discussion_comments.comment_body:
Valid and fixed in `35f2fc9393` — the same mechanism as the session id, which the cross-check confirmed: `/move` and `/wt` already insert before their transition, but the post-dispatch record runs after `getProjectDir()` changed, and the unique-prompt upsert overwrites that early insert.

Both submit paths now capture `{ sessionId, cwd }` before dispatch and pass it as one origin through `Editor.addToHistory(text, origin)` to `HistoryStorage.add`.

Verification: the attribution test now moves the working directory inside the command handler and asserts the record carries the pre-dispatch directory and session; it fails when either is dropped.

**should-fix:** This stores a snapshot, not the live value promised by the new `ExtensionContext` contract. The same command context exposes `switchSession()`, `newSession()`, `branch()`, and `navigateTree()`; after a handler awaits one of those, `ctx.activePersonaName` still reports the persona from before the operation. Please expose a getter here, as `ExtensionRunner.createContext()` does, and cover switch-then-read behavior.

Fixed in 51c5b532c. `ExtensionContext.activePersonaName` was already a live getter, but every consumer flattened it via an object-literal spread — `ExtensionRunner.createCommandContext()` spread `this.createContext()`, the non-extension-runner branch of `AgentSession#createCommandContext()` assigned the plain value, and `#tryExecuteCustomCommand()`'s `HookCommandContext` re-spread the base ctx again. Each spread copies the accessor's current value as a data property, losing liveness. All three sites now re-declare `get activePersonaName()` after the spread. Covered by a switch-then-read regression test on `ExtensionRunner.createCommandContext()` (captures the context once, mutates the underlying persona ref, re-reads the same object) and an end-to-end test that drives a real custom command through `session.prompt()`, switching persona while the handler is parked mid-await.

**should-fix:** This fire-and-forget prime cannot guarantee the first Tab works. `#hasPrimaryAgents` starts `false`; if input arrives while `discoverAgents()` is pending, `onCyclePersonaForward` calls the in-flight no-op refresh and returns `false`, routing that first press to autocomplete. The next press cycles only after discovery settles. Please represent `unknown` separately or seed/await discovery, with a delayed-discovery regression test for the first keypress.

Fixed in c74fd214d. `#hasPrimaryAgents` is now `boolean | undefined`, with `undefined` meaning the eager prime hasn't resolved yet — distinct from a known-empty project. The Tab/Shift+Tab guards now only fall through to autocomplete on `#hasPrimaryAgents === false`; a press during the still-unknown window instead routes into `cyclePersona()`, which runs its own fresh discovery rather than bouncing off the in-flight-refresh no-op. Added a delayed-discovery regression test that holds the eager prime's `discoverAgents()` call unresolved, fires the Tab handler, and asserts it does NOT return `false` (i.e. doesn't misroute to autocomplete) and that `applyAgentPersona` is eventually called once discovery settles.

**blocking** — the wall-clock bound only holds when the direct child owns the stdout pipe. On timeout this SIGKILLs `proc` (the leader only, not its group, so `detached` adds nothing here), then `await new Response(proc.stdout).text()` waits for EOF. Any descendant that inherited stdout keeps the read pending past `timeoutMs`; a wedged one keeps it pending indefinitely, which is the #8402 failure this PR targets.

Repro on this branch:
```
await runHostProbe(["sh","-c","sleep 3 & exec sleep 60"], 25)
// -> undefined, elapsed 3002 ms
```
The same command through `ptree.exec(cmd, { timeout: 25, allowNonZero: true, allowAbort: true, detached: true })` from `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils` returns in 27 ms. Its `attachTimeout` (`packages/utils/src/ptree.ts:576`) kills the process group and cancels the pending pipe readers. `tmux.ts:32-45` and `open.ts:43-56` copy this same pattern, so all three probes have the same gap.

Fixed in d27af38489 — the startup probes now go through the shared bounded-process helper `packages/coding-agent/src/utils/bounded-probe.ts` (`probeStdout`), which wraps `ptree.exec`: at the deadline the whole process group is killed and the pending pipe readers are cancelled, so a descendant that inherited stdout cannot hold the read open, and the RESULT is delivered by the deadline even when the child cannot be reaped. `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/utils/bounded-probe.test.ts` -> 11 pass / 0 fail, including the descendant-inherits-stdout case and a new test that a probe whose exit promise never settles still returns at its deadline (RED on revert: it hangs until the 5 s test timeout without the fix).

+import { ptree } from "@oh-my-pi/pi-utils";
+
+/**
+ * Wall-clock ceiling for a best-effort host probe.
+ *
+ * WSL→Windows interop can wedge indefinitely (issue #8402). A probe only ever
+ * augments the result with an extra candidate — the host home, or the Windows
+ * path an opener needs — so a few hundred milliseconds is a generous ceiling:
+ * past it the host counts as unavailable and the caller falls back to the
+ * Linux paths.
+ */
+const PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 500;
+
+/**
+ * Run a best-effort probe and return its trimmed stdout, or `undefined` when
+ * the command fails, produces no output, or exceeds the timeout.
+ *
+ * `ptree.exec` owns the wall-clock bound: at the deadline it kills the whole
+ * process group and cancels the pending pipe readers, so neither a wedged
+ * interop pipe nor a descendant that inherited stdout can hold the read open
+ * past `timeoutMs` (issue #8402). The killed/non-zero/blank outcomes all report
+ * "unavailable", and the caller falls back to the Linux candidates.
+ *
+ * This is the single entry point for startup probes — the host-discovery
+ * probes in `discovery/agents.ts` and the WSL path conversion in
+ * `utils/open.ts` share it instead of forking their own spawn/timeout logic.
+ */
+export async function runBoundedProbe(cmd: string[], timeoutMs = PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS): Promise<string | undefined> {

discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in d27af38489 — the helper no longer awaits the child's exit promise. `runBoundedProcess` races the result delivery against the wall-clock deadline, so a child that stays alive after SIGKILL (the wedged WSL interop case) cannot hold the caller open; the process-group kill and the pipe-reader cancellation keep running in the background. The new test 'delivers its result at the deadline even when the child never exits' asserts exactly that and is RED on revert: without the race it hangs until the 5 s test timeout (with the fix it returns in ~113 ms). `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/utils/bounded-probe.test.ts` -> 11 pass / 0 fail.

**should-fix (behaviour change, needs sign-off)** — `#refusePromptWhileDisposing()` makes `prompt()`, `promptCustomMessage()`, and `sendCustomMessage({ triggerTurn | deliverAs: "aside" })` throw once `beginDispose()` ran. Previously `#prepareAgentStart` (line 8803, `alreadyDisposing`) admitted a direct prompt on a disposing session, and three existing tests (`agent-session-retry-cap`, `cost-gate`, `task/prompt-cache`) had to be migrated because they relied on it. This changes a public SDK/RPC/ACP contract; per repo policy it needs explicit maintainer approval and should be its own reviewable change rather than one item among ~30 in this PR.

**should-fix:** This outcome write occurs after the `finally` block has called `finalizeSubagentLifecycle()`, which publishes the reusable ref as `idle` (`executor.ts:3547-3561`, `2600-2613`). A follow-up can therefore start, clear the verdict, and then have this older run write its result back onto the same session. Record the verdict before exposing the ref as reusable, or guard it with a per-run generation; session identity alone cannot distinguish consecutive turns on the same reusable session.

**blocking** `setStatus(..., "aborted")` does not terminate the adopted lifecycle. For an idle adopted child, the existing TTL remains armed: this event path clears neither `adopted.timer` nor `#adopted`, and `park()` later unconditionally changes the ref to `parked`, making it revivable through `ensureLive()`. I reproduced this with `idleTtlMs: 1`; after aborting the parent the child ended as `{ status: "parked", sessionAttached: false, disposed: 1 }`. A running follow-up child can also be changed back to `idle` by the persistent `agent_end` subscriber at `executor.ts:2538-2544` after this fire-and-forget abort. Please make descendant termination cancel lifecycle ownership/timers and settle abort plus disposal/detachment while preserving the terminal status.

Fixed. `release()` now snapshots the exact registered subtree, marks each current descendant aborted, performs terminal cleanup, and unregisters only the root. Exact-ref checks prevent a stale release from affecting a replacement generation.

`attachSession()` now rejects an exact ref once it is terminally aborted, before mutating the session or session-file fields. The regression verifies a late SDK attach cannot revive or alter that ref.

**blocking:** `normalizeSessionFile()` makes lock identity depend on what `realpathSync()` resolves at that moment. `FileSessionStorage.writeTextAtomic()` publishes via rename (`session-storage.ts:272`), which replaces a symlink session path; afterward the same path normalizes to the alias rather than the former target. A second writer can then acquire `<alias>.lock` while the first still holds `<target>.lock`—I reproduced both handles live simultaneously. Please use an identity stable across atomic replacement and add an integration test for a symlinked session followed by a rewrite.
Canonicalized existing session files to their real path and made atomic rewrites target that canonical file, preserving symlink aliases.

`dropSession()` now acquires the target session lock before deleting a non-current file, retains the current session lock, and releases the temporary target lock afterward; regression coverage rejects deletion while another manager owns the target.

The unsupported hard-link path now inspects the existing sidecar: live or suspect ownership is rejected as locked, malformed ownership remains fail-closed, and only missing or stale ownership permits lock-free deletion. Regression coverage acquires ownership before creating the hard link and verifies a second manager cannot delete the active session.

**blocking** — In the real event order this `settle()` call always sees `#prediction === undefined`, so no `composer_prediction_outcome` entry is ever written.

`agentLoop` pushes `agent_start` before `runLoop` emits `turn_start` and the input `message_start` events (`packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts:656`, then `emitInputMessages`). `#handleAgentStart` calls `this.composerPrediction.cancel()` (`event-controller.ts:1210`), and that sets `#prediction = undefined`. When the user's `message_start` reaches this line, `settle()` returns early at `if (!prediction ...)`.

I confirmed the order with a throwaway `Agent` + `createMockModel` probe: `agent_start -> turn_start -> message_start:user -> message_end:user -> message_start:assistant`.

The new tests call `controller.settle()` directly and never run the `agent_start` → `message_start` sequence, so they pass while the production path does nothing. Two possible fixes:
- `cancel()` (or a separate hide path used by `#handleAgentStart`) hides the ghost but keeps the ready prediction until it is settled or superseded by the next `request()`.
- settle from the submit path, before the run starts.

Either way, please add a test that drives `agent_start` and then a user `message_start` through `EventController` (or at least calls `cancel()` before `settle()` in the controller test).

Fixed in 57c3fe4d09: `#handleAgentStart` now calls `hide()`, which aborts and hides the ghost but keeps the ready prediction for `settle()`; `cancel()` still discards. Added `test/event-controller-composer-prediction.test.ts`, which drives `agent_start` then the user `message_start` through `EventController.handleEvent`; it failed before the fix and passes now.

Fixed in c073e288da: from before a new worktree is listed until its post-checkout hook is done, it carries a setup mark (`omp-setup` in its admin dir) naming the omp process setting it up (pid plus a pid-scope tag). `pr_checkout` refuses to reuse a worktree whose setting-up process is alive, or on another host or container, before changing anything; once that process is gone (it crashed mid-setup), it takes the worktree over and clears the mark. Git's own `initializing` lock is still written while the worktree is created and lifted before the hook, as `git worktree add` does, so the hook can still lock, move or remove its worktree, and ending the setup never touches a lock the hook set. The discard clears the mark and prunes the registration, also when the hook deleted `.git` and a checkout around the worktree was found instead. Tests: while the hook runs, the hook can lock its worktree and the listed worktree names this process as setup owner; a worktree marked by a live process is refused and left untouched, one marked by an exited process is reused and unmarked (on the previous commit both were reused as they were); with `worktree.base` inside another checkout, an aborted hook that deleted `.git` leaves no registration behind. Also checked on Windows.

Fixed in efe1aa01cc: the rollback now re-checks the setup mark of the worktree it finds at the saved git dir before doing anything; one carrying another process's mark is treated as gone, like a missing one, so there is no discard, no rename deletion and no branch restore. Test: a hook removes its worktree, re-adds the same branch at the same path with another owner's mark, then blocks; after the abort the replacement is still listed with that mark, its files and its branch. On the previous commit the abort force-removed it.

Fixed in d99f7386ba: when the rollback can't read the worktree listing to check the setup mark, ownership counts as unverified: nothing is discarded, no branch is deleted or restored, and a warning names the path and branch; the original error is still thrown. Test: a `/wt` setup aborted while its hook runs, with the listing failing after the abort; the worktree stays registered and on disk and its branch stays. On the previous commit the rollback removed the worktree. (Since d1d2021433 the listing also skips an entry another process is still registering, so that race no longer fails the whole listing.)

**should-fix** — this flag stays set for the whole `agent.continue(signal)` run, not only the first request after the refusal. `syncContextBeforeModelCall` runs `#runBeforeModelCallHooks` before every model call in the loop (`packages/agent/src/agent.ts:1951-1952`). Once the continued turn emits tool calls, every later model call in that run also skips usage-aware preflight, and so does the queued-message dequeue hook at line 2172. A long agentic continuation can therefore run into a usage limit that preflight would have routed around. The stated invariant is "don't split one partial response across models", so clear the suppression after the first model call (e.g. one-shot: the hook resets it on first hit) instead of on `continue()` return.

Fixed in b1be3a120b. The before-model hook now consumes the suppression flag on the first continuation request; the queue-dequeue hook only observes it until that request. Later model calls run normal usage-aware preflight. The new regression asserts `primary -> primary refusal continuation -> fallback for queued work`. The retry/fallback suite passes 156/156.
